name: bitchx
why: A scriptable IRC client from the nineties with its own scripting language, a relic of an older internet culture.

brief.what_it_is: BitchX is a free, scriptable IRC (Internet Relay Chat) client for UNIX-like systems. You run it in a terminal and point it at IRC servers and channels. The homepage describes it as a full-featured, scriptable client. SourceForge says it is based on ircII/EPIC4 and includes features that are usually added through scripts, such as CDCC and flood protection. The current release on the homepage is 1.2.1, dated 2014-11-14.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated motivation. SourceForge frames it as a more complete ircII/EPIC4-derived client, with common features built in instead of left to user scripts: you can "just start it and go."
brief.how_it_works: The client is written in C and Tcl, according to SourceForge's additional details. Its scripting layer is what the homepage calls "scriptable." I did not see the mechanism described in any fetched page, so I can't say more about how scripts are loaded or run.
brief.install_notes: The fetched pages say nothing about installation beyond the package name. The Homebrew listing names three executables: BitchX, BitchX-1.2.1, and scr-bx. I did not confirm what scr-bx does. No accounts, hardware, or first-run configuration were mentioned in what I read.
brief.standout: Most IRC clients keep scripting and extras separate. BitchX builds CDCC transfers and flood protection into the core, and it is also scriptable, which makes it a late-1990s-style power-user client that is still distributed.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage's latest release is 1.2.1 from 2014-11-14. The SourceForge page shows a last update of 2020-08-21, and its description says "Development was on hiatus for a while but is now resuming." I found no recent release or commit information, so "quiet" is my reading rather than a confirmed state.
brief.caveats: I did not fetch a README, docs, or changelog. The homepage is thin and only lists release links, so command-level detail is missing. The SourceForge rating of 5/5 rests on one review. The scout note calls it a relic of older internet culture; that is an editorial judgment and I did not verify it. The license is listed as BSD on SourceForge. The project is for UNIX-like systems, so Windows is not supported as far as I can tell.
quotes: a full-featured, scriptable free software IRC client for UNIX-like systems.
It includes many features that are usually relegated to scripts such as CDCC and flood protection -- you can just start it and go.
Development was on hiatus for a while but is now resuming.
